findings.description: The repair is sound and text and check now agree, but the orchestrator's suspicion is correct and worth recording before a worker starts: on the likely artifact the walking half never fires, because C-7's four cases need only two scratch scopes (case one must fail, cases two through four can share one passing scope) and both can sit under a single added trap, which collapses "walk every added trap in order" and "confirm the last one carries every scratch path the job creates" onto the same assertion.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:133-134. With one added trap the baseline is the file's last pre-existing trap at tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh:1203 (16 paths), and both halves reduce to comparing the job's single trap against it. This is insurance that costs nothing rather than a defect — the clause's own failing example ('a new scope whose trap lists only itself') is exactly the one-trap failure the surviving half still catches.

findings.description: One phrase could send a literal-minded checker to `blocked` rather than to a verdict: "Judge only the traps this job adds" sits beside an instruction that requires reading the pre-existing trap at `:1203` to establish the baseline for the job's first added trap, and a checker could read the first sentence as forbidding it to consult `:1203` at all, leaving that comparison undefined.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:134. Optional one-phrase repair: state that the baseline for the job's first added trap is the file's last pre-existing trap at `:1203`, whose 16 paths exclude the two known gaps. Non-blocking — 'the trap immediately preceding it' already resolves to `:1203` unambiguously for a checker that reads the whole clause.

findings.description: The rewritten grep bullet is accurate on mechanism, scope, and remedy, but its closing sentence overstates: "Every other check avoids the wrapper already, by using `ls` or no grep at all" is false of C-4, whose own check pipes lint output through `grep -E`, and the reason C-4 is safe is not avoidance but neutralization — the `| sort` immediately after makes output order irrelevant before `diff` ever sees it.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:15 against constitution.md:107, `bash "$1/inbox-to-memory/scripts/lint-scope.sh" "$d" 2>&1 | grep -E '^(RECURRING|v1 files|v2 files|total files|failures)' | sort`. Verified harmless: C-4 printed 'diff=0' on this round's run and on six consecutive runs last round.
